It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}. {{nihongo|'''Kushida Shrine, Imizu'''|櫛田神社 (射水市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Etchū Province]].

It is worshiped as a deity of marital harmony, family harmony, and matchmaking.

== Enshrined deities ==
With {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|abstract|Q272993|ar|سوسانو|azb|سوسانو|bcl|Susanoo|be|Сусанаа|bg|Сусаноо|ca|Susanoo|cs|Susanoo|da|Susa-no-o|de|Susanoo|el|Σουσάνoο|eo|Susanoo|es|Susanoo|eu|Susanoo|fa|سوسانو (خدا)|fi|Susanoo|fr|Susanoo|hr|Susano|hu|Szuszanoo|hy|Սուսանո|id|Susanoo|it|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ|ka|სუსანოო-ნო-მიკოტო|ko|스사노오|la|Susano'o|lb|Susanoo|mni|ꯁꯨꯁꯅꯨ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|nl|Susanoo|pl|Susanoo|pt|Susanoo|ro|Susanoo|rsk|Сусано|ru|Сусаноо|simple|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|sl|Susanovo|sr|Сусаноо|su|Susanoo|sv|Susanoo|ta|சுசானவோ|th|ซูซาโนโอะ|tok|jan sewi Susano|tr|Susanoo|uk|Сусаноо|vi|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|zh|素戔嗚尊|zh_min_nan|Susanoo|qid=Q272993|lt=Take-Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|Kushinadahime|de|Kushinadahime|es|Kushinadahime|fr|Kushinada-hime|it|Kushinadahime|ja|クシナダヒメ|mni|ꯀꯨꯁꯤꯅꯗꯍꯤꯃꯦ|ru|Кусинада-химэ|simple|Kushinadahime|sr|Кушинадахиме|zh|櫛名田比賣|qid=Q505469|lt=Kushinadahime-no-Mikoto}} as main {{ill|Saijin|abstract|Q11591100|fr|Saijin|ja|祭神|zh|祭神|qid=Q11591100}}, the following historical figures are additionally enshrined.

* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu-kōdaijin}}
* {{ill|Sukunabikona|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|qid=Q3275687}}

However, the 'Old shrine records and similar in Etchū Province' records the deity as Ōwakago-no-Mikoto. Ōwakago-no-Mikoto is another name of Ōhatahushi-no-Ōkami, main deity of {{ill|Kushida Shrine|Q865839|qid=Q865839|lt=Kushida Shrine}} in Chikuzen Province.

== History ==
Shrine tradition says it was founded by invitation from Takeuchi no Sukune in the age of {{ill|Emperor Chūai|Q179971|qid=Q179971}}.

A local legend says a giant serpent lived in a large nearby pond and ate villagers. One time, when it ate a girl, the comb in her hair lodged in its throat and it died; worship of the girl and the comb is said to have begun this shrine.

It is listed as "Kushida Shrine, Imizu District, Etchū Province" in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}.

== Other ==
Because stained-glass artist {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōtomo Fumiya}} from Imizu had deep attachment to this shrine in life, amulets embroidered with stained-glass motifs are produced.
